mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through lower cost of capital for corporate valuation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.5% signals labor market tightness that accelerates wage inflation and triggers monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 90th percentile.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% over 3 months) increases discount rates and reduces liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals sustained economic expansion that boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 exceeds 16000.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing production index (INDPRO) above 108.0 indicates industrial overheating that may trigger inflation and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 108.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicate accelerating labor market strength that fuels wage inflation and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases by >100k and UNRATE declines by >0.2pp in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 900.0 and RSAFS > 450000.0) indicates economic maturity with overvaluation risks, triggering monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 900.0 and RSAFS exceeds 450000.0.
